name: @qsrahman/fs-mcp-server

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file. Output is capped at about 100,000 characters; when a file is longer the result ends with the offset to continue from. Use offset and limit to read a range of lines, head for the first N lines, or tail for the last N lines (use only one of the three).

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based).

limit.description: Most lines to return, counting from offset.

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. A failed read of one file does not stop the others. Output is capped at about 200,000 characters in total; a file that does not fit is cut, with the offset to continue from with read_file.

paths.description: Paths of the files to read.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file, creating any missing parent directories. Overwrites without warning; to change part of an existing file use edit_file.

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file, written as given.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Edits apply in order, each replacing oldText with newText. oldText must match exactly one place (include enough surrounding lines to be unique), or set replaceAll to replace every match. Line endings and leading/trailing whitespace on whole lines are ignored when there is no exact match. If any edit has no match or an ambiguous one, nothing is written. Returns a git-style diff.

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

replaceAll.description: Replace every match of oldText. By default oldText must match exactly one place.

edits.description: The replacements to make, applied in order. Each oldText must match exactly one place unless replaceAll is set.

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

tools.name: shell
tools.description: Run a shell command and return its stdout, stderr and exit code as JSON. Use for tests, type checks, builds, git and similar. Do NOT use it to read, write or edit files (use the file tools), for interactive commands (stdin is closed), for commands that never exit (dev servers, watch modes), or for destructive ones (rm -rf, git reset --hard, force pushes) unless the user asked for them. Each call is a fresh process, so cd does not persist: use cwd (default: the server's working directory). The command and any processes it started are killed after timeoutMs. Past 20000 characters stdout and stderr each keep their start and end and omit the middle; binary output is replaced by a short note.

command.description: The command to run, for example 'ls -lh' or 'git status'.

cwd.description: Directory to run the command in. Defaults to the server's working directory.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the command after this many milliseconds. Defaults to 30000; 0 disables the timeout.

instructions:
File access is not restricted to particular directories. Relative paths resolve against /pkg.
- Read a file before changing it. Long files are returned in parts of about 100,000 characters; use read_file offset and limit to move through one, or head and tail for its ends.
- Change an existing file with edit_file (small, exact replacements) rather than rewriting it with write_file. Run edit_file with dryRun first when unsure.
- write_file replaces the whole file and creates missing directories.
- The shell tool runs commands with the same access as this server. Do not use it for file edits the file tools can do, or for destructive commands the user did not ask for.
